claim.statement: Kimera-SWM's PrimeTopologyWalker — the substrate's reasoning organ — has exactly four oscillator-gated operators and three halt reasons, documented verbatim at prime_topology_walker.py:1-28, 90-93, 512-660. The Walker has no autonomous decisions; every action is a reactive interpretation of a CognitiveRhythm (Cronos) oscillator signal.
claim.operationalization: Four operators (per-step): M1 COMMIT when leader_band=='gamma' (Stuart-Landau Hopf, Deco 2017); M2 HALT amplitude_death when Routh-Hurwitz delay τ > τ_crit=1/(4ω) debounced (Reddy/Sen/Johnston 1998); M3 ROLLBACK when hallucinating==True (Allan deviation slope > 0, novel application of Allan 1966); M4 LATERAL LEAP when annealing_active==True (Kirkpatrick 1983 phase-kick). Three halt reasons: amplitude_death (M2 fired), exhausted (visited all nodes), selective (step budget exhausted before all nodes visited). Verification: M.46 corpus of 515 cycles shows halt reasons are exactly the predicted subset (plus 1 'no-partition' edge case from probe-level error, unrelated to Walker physics).

claim.h1: Walker halt vocabulary matches the predicted model
